Env vars are injected at pod start. Save changes here and then redeploy this app to roll the new values out to every replica. Secret values are encrypted at rest and masked in this UI; to change one, just set it again.

postgrespassword 	{password} 	
postgresport 	{port} 	
postgresuser 	{user} 	 
some details about this database 
it is on a free dev tier at clever-cloud dot com 
it uses postgresql 18 
it allows up to five connections 
processor and memory are shared 
disk size is 256MB 
so you can imagine, very basic specs
however, it still gives us enough to build a demo project 
we will build a new set of web api endpoints 
and a new page to show the results of this web api endpoints
and to explain how to use the API endpoints 
there is no authentication needed to use these endpoints
the web api endpoint will accept http post 
and return a uuid-v7 guid or something 
and then the client will be able to get what they sent us with the guid with http get
if it still exists with us otherwise they will get a 404 not found
there should also be aggregate endpoints 
where clients can get aggregate all the data they have sent us 
based on their referer and their key
it will record the header, body, referer, all the information that the client sends 
and it presents it on the page 
each post request has a very generoud body limit maybe 10k characters or something obscenely large
the idea is to use this small database 
but old data still gets removed 
so we stay within the limits 
and as always both the web api and the page should work somewhat even if the database connection is not working 
we will lose state for some time but we should be back when the backend becomes available again 
resilience is key 
as for the uses of these new endpoints 
think demonstrating analytics, csp report only, page visit count, page visitor reaction count, or anything else 
somehow we also need to delete older entries as the database fills up before it is FULL 
we are stuck with dotnet 10 for now so we have to use packages that work with dotnet 10 
use dapper where necessary 
avoid ef core 
also there might be nuget packages and github actions 
and other dependencies that we can upgrade to latest stable as well
upgrade them all 
as we do all of this 
please be mindful to use best engineering practices 
and solid principles

The Beacons API, the `/beacons` page and the storage clean-up are written, but I couldn't compile or run the C#: this sandbox has no .NET SDK and can't reach NuGet. The SQL did run correctly against a local PostgreSQL 16 (schema, totals, per-referer and hourly counts, multi-key counts, and the size-based delete). Please build it once (`dotnet build` / `dotnet run --project Zen.Blazor`) before you push.

Extract the archive at the repo root. It only contains files that changed or are new, and nothing needs deleting.

**Changed:** `README.md`, `.github/workflows/velixir.yml`, `Zen.Blazor/Program.cs`, `Zen.Blazor/Zen.Blazor.csproj`, `Zen.Blazor/appsettings.json`, `Zen.Blazor/Components/_Imports.razor`, and `MainLayout.razor` plus its `.css` (adds a Beacons link).
**New:** 16 files in `Zen.Blazor/Beacons/`, plus `Components/Pages/BeaconBoard.razor` and its `.css`.

**Endpoints** (no authentication, CORS open):

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/beacons/{key}` | Stores the request; returns 201 with a UUIDv7 id and a `Location` header |
| GET | `/api/entries/{id}` | Returns everything recorded, or 404 if it's gone |
| GET | `/api/beacons/{key}?referer=` | Totals, top referers, and hourly counts for the last 24 hours |
| GET | `/api/beacons/{key}/entries` | Lists entries, newest first, with paging |
| GET | `/api/beacons` | Busiest keys |
| GET | `/api/status` | Database and memory health |

**How it behaves:**
- **Requests:** bodies can be up to 32 KiB. Headers, body, referer, user agent, method, path and query are recorded. IP addresses are cut to /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), and `Cookie`, `Authorization` and forwarding headers are blanked out, because everything stored is publicly readable.
- **When the database is down:** writes land in a capped in-memory buffer (4 MiB) first, and a background writer saves them to Postgres in batches. If the database is down, reads use memory and say `degraded: true`. The writer keeps retrying, waiting longer each time up to 60 seconds. A lookup for an id that isn't in memory returns 503 with a `Retry-After` header instead of a false 404.
- **Staying under the 256 MB disk:**
  - Every 2 minutes, entries older than 30 days are deleted.
  - If stored data passes 48 MiB, the oldest entries are removed until it's back to about 80% of that.
  - If the whole database passes 160 MiB and is still growing, the 48 MiB limit is halved and the table is vacuumed.
  - All of these limits are settings in `appsettings.json`.
- **Connections:** each app instance opens at most 2 of the 5 database connections. It builds the connection from your `postgreshost`, `postgresport`, `postgresdatabase`, `postgresuser` and `postgrespassword` variables, and uses `postgresconnectionstring` only if those are missing. The table is created on first use.
- **Limits:** each IP can make 30 writes and 120 reads per minute.
- **Demo page:** `/beacons` counts visits, has four reaction buttons with live counts, and shows recent entries, top keys and copy-paste examples (curl, `sendBeacon`, CSP).
- **CSP demo:** every page now sends a report-only Content Security Policy. Violation reports go to the key `zen-csp`, so they also count against the storage limits.

**Upgrades:**
- Added Dapper 2.1.89 and Npgsql 10.0.3, the latest stable versions. Npgsql 10 targets .NET 10. These are the first third-party packages in the project.
- `actions/checkout@v7` was already the latest.
- I added a build job (`actions/setup-dotnet@v6`) that must pass before deploy. Pull requests now build but don't deploy.
- I removed the one comment that was in the workflow file.

Sources:
- [Npgsql on NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Npgsql)
- [Dapper on NuGet](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Dapper)
- [actions/checkout releases](https://github.com/actions/checkout/releases)
- [actions/setup-dotnet releases](https://github.com/actions/setup-dotnet/releases)
- [Dapper + Npgsql `ANY(@array)`](https://dev.to/ankursheel/how-to-write-a-query-with-the-in-operator-using-dapper-and-npgsql-4cg0)

























































Claude

where clients can get aggregate all the data they have sent us 
based on their referer and their key
it will record the header, body, referer, all the information that the client sends 
and it presents it on the page 
each post request has a very generoud body limit maybe 10k characters or something obscenely large
the idea is to use this small database 
but old data still gets removed 
so we stay within the limits 
and as always both the web api and the page should work somewhat even if the database connection is not working 
we will lose state for some time but we should be back when the backend becomes available again 
resilience is key 
as for the uses of these new endpoints 
think demonstrating analytics, csp report only, page visit count, page visitor reaction count, or anything else 
somehow we also need to delete older entries as the database fills up before it is FULL 
we are stuck with dotnet 10 for now so we have to use packages that work with dotnet 10 
use dapper where necessary 
avoid ef core 
also there might be nuget packages and github actions 
and other dependencies that we can upgrade to latest stable as well
upgrade them all 
as we do all of this 
please be mindful to use best engineering practices 
and solid principles

Changed: README.md, .github/workflows/velixir.yml, Zen.Blazor/Program.cs, Zen.Blazor/Zen.Blazor.csproj, Zen.Blazor/appsettings.json, Zen.Blazor/Components/_Imports.razor, and MainLayout.razor plus its .css (adds a Beacons link).
New: 16 files in Zen.Blazor/Beacons/, plus Components/Pages/BeaconBoard.razor and its .css.

Endpoints (no authentication, CORS open):

Method	Path	What it does
POST	/api/beacons/{key}	Stores the request; returns 201 with a UUIDv7 id and a Location header
GET	/api/entries/{id}	Returns everything recorded, or 404 if it’s gone
GET	/api/beacons/{key}?referer=	Totals, top referers, and hourly counts for the last 24 hours
GET	/api/beacons/{key}/entries	Lists entries, newest first, with paging
GET	/api/beacons	Busiest keys
GET	/api/status	Database and memory health
How it behaves:

Requests: bodies can be up to 32 KiB. Headers, body, referer, user agent, method, path and query are recorded. IP addresses are cut to /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), and Cookie, Authorization and forwarding headers are blanked out, because everything stored is publicly readable.
When the database is down: writes land in a capped in-memory buffer (4 MiB) first, and a background writer saves them to Postgres in batches. If the database is down, reads use memory and say degraded: true. The writer keeps retrying, waiting longer each time up to 60 seconds. A lookup for an id that isn’t in memory returns 503 with a Retry-After header instead of a false 404.
Staying under the 256 MB disk:
Every 2 minutes, entries older than 30 days are deleted.
If stored data passes 48 MiB, the oldest entries are removed until it’s back to about 80% of that.
If the whole database passes 160 MiB and is still growing, the 48 MiB limit is halved and the table is vacuumed.
All of these limits are settings in appsettings.json.
Connections: each app instance opens at most 2 of the 5 database connections. It builds the connection from your postgreshost, postgresport, postgresdatabase, postgresuser and postgrespassword variables, and uses postgresconnectionstring only if those are missing. The table is created on first use.
Limits: each IP can make 30 writes and 120 reads per minute.
Demo page: /beacons counts visits, has four reaction buttons with live counts, and shows recent entries, top keys and copy-paste examples (curl, sendBeacon, CSP).
CSP demo: every page now sends a report-only Content Security Policy. Violation reports go to the key zen-csp, so they also count against the storage limits.
Upgrades:

Added Dapper 2.1.89 and Npgsql 10.0.3, the latest stable versions. Npgsql 10 targets .NET 10. These are the first third-party packages in the project.
actions/checkout@v7 was already the latest.
I added a build job (actions/setup-dotnet@v6) that must pass before deploy. Pull requests now build but don’t deploy.
I removed the one comment that was in the workflow file.
Sources:

Npgsql on NuGet
Dapper on NuGet
actions/checkout releases
actions/setup-dotnet releases
Dapper + Npgsql ANY(@array)

**Changed:** README.md, .github/workflows/velixir.yml, Zen.Blazor/Program.cs, Zen.Blazor/Zen.Blazor.csproj, Zen.Blazor/appsettings.json, Zen.Blazor/Components/_Imports.razor, and MainLayout.razor plus its .css (adds a Beacons link).
**New:** 16 files in Zen.Blazor/Beacons/, plus Components/Pages/BeaconBoard.razor and its .css.

**Endpoints** (no authentication, CORS open):

| Method | Path | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| POST | /api/beacons/{key} | Stores the request; returns 201 with a UUIDv7 id and a Location header |
| GET | /api/entries/{id} | Returns everything recorded, or 404 if it's gone |
| GET | /api/beacons/{key}?referer= | Totals, top referers, and hourly counts for the last 24 hours |
| GET | /api/beacons/{key}/entries | Lists entries, newest first, with paging |
| GET | /api/beacons | Busiest keys |
| GET | /api/status | Database and memory health |

**How it behaves:**
- **Requests:** bodies can be up to 32 KiB. Headers, body, referer, user agent, method, path and query are recorded. IP addresses are cut to /24 (IPv4) or /48 (IPv6), and Cookie, Authorization and forwarding headers are blanked out, because everything stored is publicly readable.
- **When the database is down:** writes land in a capped in-memory buffer (4 MiB) first, and a background writer saves them to Postgres in batches. If the database is down, reads use memory and say degraded: true. The writer keeps retrying, waiting longer each time up to 60 seconds. A lookup for an id that isn't in memory returns 503 with a Retry-After header instead of a false 404.
- **Staying under the 256 MB disk:**
  - Every 2 minutes, entries older than 30 days are deleted.
  - If stored data passes 48 MiB, the oldest entries are removed until it's back to about 80% of that.
  - If the whole database passes 160 MiB and is still growing, the 48 MiB limit is halved and the table is vacuumed.
  - All of these limits are settings in appsettings.json.
- **Connections:** each app instance opens at most 2 of the 5 database connections. It builds the connection from your postgreshost, postgresport, postgresdatabase, postgresuser and postgrespassword variables, and uses postgresconnectionstring only if those are missing. The table is created on first use.
- **Limits:** each IP can make 30 writes and 120 reads per minute.
- **Demo page:** /beacons counts visits, has four reaction buttons with live counts, and shows recent entries, top keys and copy-paste examples (curl, sendBeacon, CSP).
- **CSP demo:** every page now sends a report-only Content Security Policy. Violation reports go to the key zen-csp, so they also count against the storage limits.

**Upgrades:**
- Added Dapper 2.1.89 and Npgsql 10.0.3, the latest stable versions. Npgsql 10 targets .NET 10. These are the first third-party packages in the project.
- actions/checkout@v7 was already the latest.
- I added a build job (actions/setup-dotnet@v6) that must pass before deploy. Pull requests now build but don't deploy.
- I removed the one comment that was in the workflow file.

Read 4 pages, searched the web, and 3 more tools
The code isn’t what’s blocking the connection. velixir blocks it at the network level. Their Limits and fair use page says apps can only make outbound connections on ports 443 and 80, plus DNS and velixir’s own managed Postgres/Valkey. Everything else is blocked unless you ask for it. They name “an external database on 5432” as something support will open if you file a ticket.

That’s why switching Clever Cloud for Neon changed nothing: both use port 5432. Your logs show the same thing. The connection failed in the same millisecond the app started, so it was refused straight away rather than timing out, and it reports Network is unreachable. The last address it tried was IPv6, which those pods also don’t seem to have a route for. Before that, the IPv4 attempt failed just as fast.

The app itself is behaving as designed while it can’t reach the database: everything stays in memory, responses say degraded: true, and it keeps retrying.

What to do: open a velixir support ticket to allow outbound TCP 5432 to your Clever Cloud host. After that, the existing code should connect on IPv4 with no changes. If you’d rather not file a ticket, the other routes are velixir’s own managed Postgres (paid) or Neon’s HTTP SQL API over 443. The Neon route would need a separate store class and wouldn’t use Dapper.

Code changes are only to make this obvious next time:

The warning is now one line with the root cause, like SocketException:NetworkUnreachable: Network is unreachable. The full stack trace moved to Debug level.
A new warning is logged whenever the failure reason changes.
/api/status → lastError now shows the socket error code, so you can check from a browser without opening the logs.
The README notes the port restriction.
Nothing to delete. I still couldn’t compile here.

Zen.Blazor/Beacons/DatabaseCircuit.cs
csharp
using System.Net.Sockets;

namespace Zen.Blazor.Beacons;

public readonly record struct CircuitState(int Failures, DateTimeOffset? RetryAt, DateTimeOffset? LastSuccessAt, string? LastError);

public sealed class DatabaseCircuit(TimeProvider time, ILogger<DatabaseCircuit> logger)
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan MinDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2);
    private static readonly TimeSpan MaxDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60);

    private readonly Lock _gate = new();
    private int _failures;
    private DateTimeOffset _retryAt = DateTimeOffset.MinValue;
    private DateTimeOffset? _lastSuccessAt;
    private string? _lastError;

    public bool CanAttempt
    {
        get
        {
            lock (_gate)
            {
                return time.GetUtcNow() >= _retryAt;
            }
        }
    }

    public TimeSpan RetryIn
    {
        get
        {
            lock (_gate)
            {
                var wait = _retryAt - time.GetUtcNow();
                return wait > TimeSpan.Zero ? wait : TimeSpan.Zero;
            }
        }
    }

    public CircuitState State
    {
        get
        {
            lock (_gate)
            {
                return new CircuitState(
                    _failures,
                    _failures > 0 ? _retryAt : null,
                    _lastSuccessAt,
                    _lastError);
            }
        }
    }

    public void Succeeded()
    {
        int previous;
        lock (_gate)
        {
            previous = _failures;
            _failures = 0;
            _retryAt = DateTimeOffset.MinValue;
            _lastSuccessAt = time.GetUtcNow();
            _lastError = null;
        }

        if (previous > 0)
        {
            logger.LogWarning("Database available again after {Failures} failed attempts", previous);
        }
    }

    public void Failed(Exception exception)
    {
        var reason = Describe(exception);
        int failures;
        TimeSpan delay;
        bool changed;
        lock (_gate)
        {
            failures = ++_failures;
            var factor = Math.Pow(2, Math.Min(failures - 1, 10));
            delay = TimeSpan.FromTicks(Math.Min(MaxDelay.Ticks, (long)(MinDelay.Ticks * factor)));
            _retryAt = time.GetUtcNow() + delay;
            changed = _lastError != reason;
            _lastError = reason;
        }

        if (failures == 1 || changed)
        {
            logger.LogWarning(
                "Database unavailable ({Reason}: {Message}); serving from memory, retrying in {Delay}",
                reason, Innermost(exception).Message, delay);
        }

        logger.LogDebug(exception, "Database attempt {Failures} failed", failures);
    }

    private static string Describe(Exception exception)
    {
        for (var current = exception; current is not null; current = current.InnerException)
        {
            if (current is SocketException socket)
            {
                return $"{nameof(SocketException)}:{socket.SocketErrorCode}";
            }
        }

        return Innermost(exception).GetType().Name;
    }

    private static Exception Innermost(Exception exception)
    {
        var current = exception;
        while (current.InnerException is not null)
        {
            current = current.InnerException;
        }

        return current;
    }
}
README.md
markdown
# zen-velixir-run

Minimal .NET 10 Blazor Server app on the [velixir](https://zen.velixir.run/) free tier (0.25 vCPU, 256 MB).

- Live message board: anyone posts up to 500 chars, everyone connected sees it instantly. In memory only, newest 50 kept, 2 s per-visitor cooldown.
- Header shows server time, ticking every second from one shared server timer.
- Beacons (`/beacons`): public, unauthenticated capture API with a live page and usage docs. See below.
- Packages: Dapper and Npgsql only. No CSS or JS frameworks. Evergreen browsers only.
- Component styles in `*.razor.css`; globals and color tokens (`light-dark()`) in `wwwroot/app.css`.
- Binds to `PORT` when set; honors `X-Forwarded-For`/`X-Forwarded-Proto` from the edge.
- Memory cap: workstation non-concurrent GC, `ConserveMemory=7`, no tiered PGO, invariant globalization, short disconnected-circuit retention, 2 unacked render batches per circuit.
- Data protection keys are in-memory; a restart invalidates antiforgery cookies, so that log category is off. Restarts show as `Application started` in logs.
- Messages truncate on grapheme boundaries.
- Every page sends `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only`; reports land in beacon key `zen-csp`.
- Push to `main` builds then deploys via `.github/workflows/velixir.yml` (secret `VELIXIR_API_KEY`). PRs build only.

## Beacons

| Method | Path | Result |
|---|---|---|
| POST | `/api/beacons/{key}` | 201, UUIDv7 id, `Location` |
| GET | `/api/entries/{id}` | Full record or 404; 503 + `Retry-After` if DB down and not in memory |
| GET | `/api/beacons/{key}?referer=` | Total, bytes, first/last, top 25 referers, hourly 24 h |
| GET | `/api/beacons/{key}/entries?referer=&before=&limit=` | Newest first, max 100, `next` cursor |
| GET | `/api/beacons?limit=` | Busiest keys |
| GET | `/api/status` | Storage health |

- Key: `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._~:-]{0,63}$`. Body ≤ 32 KiB, any type; invalid UTF-8 or NUL stored as base64.
- Records method, path, query, referer (`Referer` else `Origin`), content type, user agent, headers, body. IP truncated to /24 or /48. `Cookie`, `Authorization` and forwarding headers redacted.
- Open CORS. Per-IP token buckets: 30 writes/min, 120 reads/min.
- Writes go to a bounded memory buffer (4 MiB / 2000 entries) and a background writer batches them into PostgreSQL. DB down: reads serve memory with `degraded: true`, writer retries with backoff (2–60 s), oldest unsaved entries drop if the buffer fills.
- Janitor every 2 min: deletes entries older than 30 days, trims oldest to 80% when stored bytes exceed 48 MiB, halves the budget and vacuums if `pg_database_size` exceeds 160 MiB and is still growing.
- Pool max 2 connections (server allows 5). Schema is created on first use.
- No PostgreSQL settings: memory only.
- velixir blocks outbound ports other than 80/443 unless opened by support ticket; an external database on 5432 needs that. Pods have no IPv6 route. `/api/status` `lastError` shows the socket error.

Settings in `appsettings.json` under `Beacons`. Connection from env vars `postgreshost`, `postgresport`, `postgresdatabase`, `postgresuser`, `postgrespassword`, or `postgresconnectionstring` (`postgresql://user:pass@host:port/db`) as fallback.

```
dotnet run --project Zen.Blazor
./export.sh
```

Now the README note.The code isn't what's blocking the connection. velixir blocks it at the network level. Their [Limits and fair use](https://velixir.net/docs/limits) page says apps can only make outbound connections on ports 443 and 80, plus DNS and velixir's own managed Postgres/Valkey. Everything else is blocked unless you ask for it. They name "an external database on 5432" as something support will open if you file a ticket.

That's why switching Clever Cloud for Neon changed nothing: both use port 5432. Your logs show the same thing. The connection failed in the same millisecond the app started, so it was refused straight away rather than timing out, and it reports `Network is unreachable`. The last address it tried was IPv6, which those pods also don't seem to have a route for. Before that, the IPv4 attempt failed just as fast.

The app itself is behaving as designed while it can't reach the database: everything stays in memory, responses say `degraded: true`, and it keeps retrying.

**What to do:** open a velixir support ticket to allow outbound TCP 5432 to your Clever Cloud host. After that, the existing code should connect on IPv4 with no changes. If you'd rather not file a ticket, the other routes are velixir's own managed Postgres (paid) or Neon's HTTP SQL API over 443. The Neon route would need a separate store class and wouldn't use Dapper.

**Code changes** are only to make this obvious next time:
- The warning is now one line with the root cause, like `SocketException:NetworkUnreachable: Network is unreachable`. The full stack trace moved to Debug level.
- A new warning is logged whenever the failure reason changes.
- `/api/status` → `lastError` now shows the socket error code, so you can check from a browser without opening the logs.
- The README notes the port restriction.

Nothing to delete. I still couldn't compile here.

### `Zen.Blazor/Beacons/DatabaseCircuit.cs`

```csharp
using System.Net.Sockets;

namespace Zen.Blazor.Beacons;

public readonly record struct CircuitState(int Failures, DateTimeOffset? RetryAt, DateTimeOffset? LastSuccessAt, string? LastError);

public sealed class DatabaseCircuit(TimeProvider time, ILogger<DatabaseCircuit> logger)
{
    private static readonly TimeSpan MinDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(2);
    private static readonly TimeSpan MaxDelay = TimeSpan.FromSeconds(60);

    private readonly Lock _gate = new();
    private int _failures;
    private DateTimeOffset _retryAt = DateTimeOffset.MinValue;
    private DateTimeOffset? _lastSuccessAt;
    private string? _lastError;

    public bool CanAttempt
    {
        get
        {
            lock (_gate)
            {
                return time.GetUtcNow() >= _retryAt;
            }
        }
    }

    public TimeSpan RetryIn
    {
        get
        {
            lock (_gate)
            {
                var wait = _retryAt - time.GetUtcNow();
                return wait > TimeSpan.Zero ? wait : TimeSpan.Zero;
            }
        }
    }

    public CircuitState State
    {
        get
        {
            lock (_gate)
            {
                return new CircuitState(
                    _failures,
                    _failures > 0 ? _retryAt : null,
                    _lastSuccessAt,
                    _lastError);
            }
        }
    }

    public void Succeeded()
    {
        int previous;
        lock (_gate)
        {
            previous = _failures;
            _failures = 0;
            _retryAt = DateTimeOffset.MinValue;
            _lastSuccessAt = time.GetUtcNow();
            _lastError = null;
        }

        if (previous > 0)
        {
            logger.LogWarning("Database available again after {Failures} failed attempts", previous);
        }
    }

    public void Failed(Exception exception)
    {
        var reason = Describe(exception);
        int failures;
        TimeSpan delay;
        bool changed;
        lock (_gate)
        {
            failures = ++_failures;
            var factor = Math.Pow(2, Math.Min(failures - 1, 10));
            delay = TimeSpan.FromTicks(Math.Min(MaxDelay.Ticks, (long)(MinDelay.Ticks * factor)));
            _retryAt = time.GetUtcNow() + delay;
            changed = _lastError != reason;
            _lastError = reason;
        }

        if (failures == 1 || changed)
        {
            logger.LogWarning(
                "Database unavailable ({Reason}: {Message}); serving from memory, retrying in {Delay}",
                reason, Innermost(exception).Message, delay);
        }

        logger.LogDebug(exception, "Database attempt {Failures} failed", failures);
    }

    private static string Describe(Exception exception)
    {
        for (var current = exception; current is not null; current = current.InnerException)
        {
            if (current is SocketException socket)
            {
                return $"{nameof(SocketException)}:{socket.SocketErrorCode}";
            }
        }

        return Innermost(exception).GetType().Name;
    }

    private static Exception Innermost(Exception exception)
    {
        var current = exception;
        while (current.InnerException is not null)
        {
            current = current.InnerException;
        }

        return current;
    }
}
```
